name: Fuchs Endothelial Corneal Dystrophy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Fuchs Endothelial Corneal Dystrophy

criteria.description: Presence of corneal endothelial guttae visible on slit-lamp examination
Central corneal stromal and epithelial edema causing thickening
Progressive decrease in visual acuity, especially in the morning
Reduced endothelial cell density and abnormal morphology on specular microscopy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of corneal endothelial guttae and corneal edema with compatible clinical findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; genetic testing is not routinely performed.

pathognomonic.notes: Visible as excrescences on Descemet membrane
searchTerms: small bumps on cornea inner layer

pathognomonic.symptomName: Central corneal stromal and epithelial edema
pathognomonic.notes: Leads to corneal thickening and haziness

common.notes: Worse in the morning due to corneal hydration changes

searchTerms: seeing glare or halos around lights

common.symptomName: Eye discomfort or foreign body sensation
searchTerms: eye irritation or feeling something in eye

occasional.notes: Occurs in advanced disease with bullous keratopathy
searchTerms: eye pain due to epithelial bullae

occasional.notes: Mild inflammation secondary to epithelial breakdown

rare.notes: Usually in late-stage disease or secondary complications
Due to angle closure from corneal edema
Extremely rare complication of advanced bullous keratopathy

imaging: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy showing endothelial guttae and corneal edema
Specular microscopy demonstrating decreased endothelial cell density and pleomorphism
Anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT) showing corneal thickening and edema
genetic: Association with TCF4 gene polymorphisms (common late-onset forms)
other: In vivo confocal microscopy revealing endothelial cell abnormalities
Pachymetry showing increased central corneal thickness

distinguishingFeatures: History of intraocular surgery or inflammation
More acute onset of corneal edema and bullae

redFlags: Rapidly worsening vision indicating possible secondary infection or acute decompensation
Severe ocular pain suggesting epithelial bullae rupture or infection
Signs of secondary glaucoma such as eye redness, headache, or elevated intraocular pressure
references: Krachmer JH, Purcell JJ, Young CW, Bucher KD. Corneal endothelial dystrophy. A study of 64 families. Arch Ophthalmol. 1978;96(11):2036-2039.
Møller HU. Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy. Acta Ophthalmol. 2018;96(1):1-2.
Afshari NA, Pittard AB, Lass JH. Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy: clinical characteristics and genetic advances. Cornea. 2017;36(5):605-610.
